issues.legal_issue: Whether profits from purchasing land, subdividing it, and selling the resulting plots constitute profits from an adventure in the nature of trade.
material_facts: The purchasers acquired land and, shortly afterward, divided it into four plots.
They sold the plots within a few months of acquiring the land.
The total sale consideration was substantially greater than the purchase price.
The tax tribunal had treated the purchase as an investment, but the High Court concluded that the purchasers intended to resell the land.
issues.conclusion: The transaction constituted an adventure in the nature of trade, and the Court found no ground to interfere with the High Court’s conclusion.
issues.legal_principle: Whether a transaction is an adventure in the nature of trade is assessed from its facts and circumstances. The prompt subdivision and resale of the land, considered with the other circumstances, were more consistent with an intention to resell than with an investment. The matter came before the High Court by reference under Section 256(1) of the Income Tax Act; the Supreme Court relied on no earlier cases in deciding this issue.

rule.if: income_tax_reference_appeal and land_subdivided_soon_after_purchase and plots_sold_within_months and resale_gain

predicates.income_tax_reference_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning a High Court’s answer to a referred income-tax question.
predicates.land_subdivided_soon_after_purchase: The purchasers divided the land into plots shortly after acquiring it.
predicates.plots_sold_within_months: The purchasers sold the plots within a few months of acquiring the land.
predicates.resale_gain: The purchasers received more for the land on resale than they had paid to acquire it.

issues.definition: When an income-tax reference appeal involves land divided soon after purchase and plots sold within months at a gain, the transaction is treated as an adventure in the nature of trade.
